corrected_afterwards: Measured 2026-11-12 in canonical/verification/PASSING_PATCH_SHAPE_SWEBENCH_VERIFIED_20261112_V1.json: the limit named here first, that a smaller change than the expert's may repair the same bug, is real and large. Among patches of recorded agents that passed the benchmark's tests, some patch is one listable small change for at least 80 of the 500 tasks (this record: 40 by the expert's fix), and some patch stays within one statement for at least 276 (this record: 169). 'About 8% for one small change' below is the share of EXPERT fixes that are such a change; as a ceiling on repairing it was too low by half or more.
read_this_first: Every way of repairing without a model that was measured here makes ONE small change to a program and lets the tests judge it. This count asks, of real fixes and with no test run, how many ARE one small change. On the benchmarks those ways were measured on, nearly all are: 59 of 64 development fixes of HumanEvalFix (92%) and 2,669 of 2,863 ConDefects fixes (93%) change at most one statement. Of the 500 expert fixes of SWE-bench Verified, read from the merged pull requests of 12 real projects, 169 (34%) do; 331 (66%) change several statements, several places or several files. A list of single small changes that knows only the buggy file could hold at most 40 of the 500 (8%): 7 one piece taken out, 20 a small piece put in, 13 one leaf exchanged. On the two benchmarks it is 38 of 64 (59%) and 1,326 of 2,863 (46%). Of the 292 larger fixes that stay in one file, 190 are written with a name or constant that file does not hold. Cut into their smallest independent pieces the 500 fixes are 2,178 pieces and 81 tasks add or remove a whole definition or file; 677 of the pieces (31%) can be listed, and for 54 tasks (11%) every piece can. So the ceiling on real projects is about 8% for one small change and about 11% for any number of them made one after another, before asking how long the lists are or whether tests could judge the pieces one at a time. Rule written beforehand, real projects: at least 50 of 500 listable, else no repair run on real projects with such lists. It came to 40: not met, so none is built. Rule written beforehand, one piece put in: at least 6 of the 64 development fixes a small piece needing nothing new. It came to 7: met; it may be built for HumanEvalFix, and was not built this turn. 5 of the 13 things expected beforehand held. No program and no test was run; no model was called. One machine, the producer's run; nobody else has re-run it.
what_was_asked: How many real fixes are one small change -- one piece taken out, one piece put in, one leaf exchanged -- and what the rest are. It is the ceiling of every family of single small changes, learned or listed, and it costs no test run to know it before another such family is built.

cut_into_pieces.how: canonical/tools/expert_fix_repetition_measure_v1.py cuts a fix into its smallest independent pieces; each piece is given its shape with 'held' meaning what the changed files held before the fix, so that a name another piece brings in does not count as held.

one piece taken out.note: known from an earlier look, not a prediction

one piece put in.rule: A family that puts one piece in is built for HumanEvalFix only if at least 6 of the 64 development fixes are one piece put in, of at most 3 nodes, written with what the program holds or Python has built in.
one piece put in.what follows: It may be built for HumanEvalFix. It was not built this turn. Its ceiling on real projects is 20 of 500, and a list of small pieces put in runs to thousands a bug.

real projects.rule: A repair run on real projects with lists of single small changes is built only if at least 50 of the 500 expert fixes can be listed. Below that such lists have their ceiling in sight there, and what comes next has to make several changes that belong together.
real projects.what follows: No repair run on real projects is built with lists of single small changes. What comes next there has to make several changes that belong together, mostly written with names the file does not hold.

one piece taken out, decided the long wa.what: fix_shape decides it from the part of the program that differs; the long way lists every candidate of take_out_v1 for the whole program and looks for the other program among them, both ways round.

60 ConDefects pairs spread over the set.run_at: an earlier state of the code (0af3d94a with the spread of pairs): before 'held' could be handed in and before the size limit went from 6,000 to 1,000 nodes. 390.5 s.

checks.against a number published elsewhere: 69 of 500 (14%) expert fixes change more than one Python file outside the tests. A page citing Epoch AI gives 14.2% of Verified tasks as needing edits to more than one file (aiwiki.ai/wiki/swe-bench_verified, read as a search result, not opened).

the count twice.what: The whole count was made once with the size limit at 6,000 nodes (the state after 0af3d94a) and once at 300 (903e88bd, the one kept). What moved is the fixes whose statement is too large to ask take_out_v1 about.

checks.found by the tests before any count was: A part that cannot be parsed made a pair look unreadable; two definitions changed side by side were called one place. Both mended at 0af3d94a; the run before it was stopped and is not kept.

what_this_does_not_show: It bounds reaching the EXPERT'S fix with one small change. Another change may repair the same bug: on the 100 scored HumanEvalFix bugs 53 repairs were right and 27 of them were the published fix. How often a smaller right repair exists for a real-project bug was not measured.
'Can be listed' is a ceiling. It says nothing of how long such a list is (thousands of candidates a bug for small pieces put in) nor whether the tests would pick the right one.
'Every piece can be listed' is a ceiling too: it does not ask whether each piece can be judged by the tests on its own, which making them one after another would need.
SWE-bench Verified is 500 tasks from 12 Python projects, 231 of them django, chosen by its authors as well specified and tested. Fixes at large are probably not smaller.
'Held' means written somewhere in the changed file, as any kind of name. For a project it is too narrow (a name held in another file counts as new) and for a place too wide.
The line between 'several statements at one place' and 'several places' is rough. The line above them, at most one statement, is not.
A statement of more than 300 nodes is not asked about; how many there were is in the count.
No program and no test was run, so nothing here says what any of these ways would repair.
One machine, the producer's run. Nobody else has re-run it.
